result:
I’ve been thinking about the way light gets stuck in things.

Not in a poetic, try-hard way. I mean literally. The way the afternoon sun will find a single dust mote in my kitchen and hold it for three seconds before moving on. The way it catches the edge of a chipped mug and makes the chip look intentional, like a design choice.

This morning I made coffee I didn’t drink. I just watched it. The steam rose and then it didn’t. The kitchen was quiet enough to hear the fridge hum change pitch when it kicked on. My neighbor’s kid was practicing drums again, very badly and very committedly, through the wall. It was 9:17 a.m. and nothing needed to happen.

I think we underestimate how much of life is made of these unaccountable pauses. We want narrative arcs, we want the plot to move. But most days are just a series of small, bright moments that don’t connect to anything. A pigeon landing on the fire escape with perfect balance. The exact blue of a bus ticket in your pocket. The smell of rain hitting hot pavement two streets over.

If you sit still long enough, the world starts offering you these things for free. No reason. No lesson.

I’m going to go walk now with no destination. I might buy a pastry I won’t finish. I might notice the light again.

It’s probably already moving.
